glossary.def: A form of data a model reads or produces: text, image, audio, video or a document page that mixes them.
A voice model that listens while it speaks, so users can interrupt or keep talking while backend work runs.
Labelling who spoke when in a recording. Azure Speech can separate up to 35 speakers.
A caller starting to speak while the agent is talking, which should stop or yield the agent's reply.
A short-lived credential minted by your server so a browser can open a realtime session without a standing API key.
A synchronous file transcription mode that returns results faster than real time with predictable latency.
A `semantic_vad` setting (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `auto`) that controls how quickly the model decides the user has finished.
The late-interaction score: for each query token take the best matching page vector, then sum.
Many vectors per item (one per patch or token) instead of one, used by ColPali and ColBERT style retrieval.
The page coordinates of extracted text or a field, used to ground and audit an extraction.
An Azure AI Content Safety feature that detects user prompt attacks and document attacks (hidden instructions in third-party content).
A text description or data table that carries the meaning of a figure for people who cannot see it.

claims.text: OpenAI image input allows up to 512 MB per request and 1,500 images per request, and rejects images over 30,000 patches instead of shrinking them.
The `detail` parameter defaults to `auto` in both the Responses API and Chat Completions.
On the gpt-5.4 family `detail: low` uses a 2048 px and 6,144-patch budget, so it can use more tokens than `high`.
Patch models use ceil(w/32) x ceil(h/32) patches, a 2,500-patch budget at `high` for gpt-5.5, and a 1.2 multiplier, rounded up.
gpt-4.1 and gpt-4o use 85 base tokens and 170 tokens per tile, and `low` costs only the base tokens.
Azure's vision chat page lists 20 MB per image and 10 images per call.

OpenAI lists vision limitations: medical images, non-Latin text, small text, rotation, varied-style graphs, spatial localisation, panoramic and fisheye shapes, approximate counts, ignored metadata, blocked CAPTCHAs.
gpt-transcribe is the recommended file transcription model, with 25 MB files in mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, wav or webm.
With gpt-transcribe `languages` replaces `language` and both must not be sent together.
gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize returns `diarized_json` and needs `chunking_strategy` for audio over 30 seconds; whisper-1 gives word timestamps and English-only translation.
gpt-4o-mini-tts accepts `instructions`, tts-1 has lower latency than tts-1-hd, and wav or pcm give the fastest response.
Azure Speech offers real-time, fast (synchronous) and batch transcription, and diarization for up to 35 speakers.
Voice Live lists over 140 locales for speech to text and over 600 standard voices across 150 or more locales.
Microsoft lists about 100 ms for WebRTC, about 200 ms for WebSocket and varying latency for SIP in Azure OpenAI realtime.
Azure realtime sessions last at most 60 minutes, use the GA /openai/v1 endpoint and send no api-version.
OpenAI mints ephemeral keys with POST /v1/realtime/client_secrets and uses /v1/realtime/calls for GA WebRTC.
Realtime audio is 1 token per 100 ms for user audio and 1 per 50 ms for assistant audio, and the conversation is resent each turn.
session.truncation.retention_ratio defaults to 1.0 and 0.8 drops extra items to keep the cache valid longer.
GPT-Live is full duplex and delegates reasoning to a separate backend through Responses delegation or client delegation.
Foundry voice agents (preview) offer native speech-to-speech and cascaded architectures, and latency_threshold_ms for interim responses defaults to 2000.
Voice Live turn_detection types are server_vad (default), semantic_vad (gpt-realtime and gpt-realtime-mini only), azure_semantic_vad and azure_semantic_vad_multilingual.
In Voice Live threshold defaults to 0.5, silence_duration_ms to 500, and remove_filler_words to false.
azure_semantic_vad_multilingual lists English, Spanish, French, Italian, German, Japanese, Portuguese, Chinese, Korean and Hindi.
OpenAI Realtime semantic_vad uses eagerness low, medium, high or auto, where auto equals medium.
The Content Understanding video analyzer samples about 1 frame per second at 512 x 512, transcribes speech only, and segmentation spends generative tokens.
Content Understanding GA is 2025-11-01, and 2026-06-01-preview adds agentic mode, in-page segmentation and signature detection with no SLA.
Document Intelligence containers are the only on-premises option, and custom models can start from as few as 5 labelled samples.
Document Intelligence v4.0 is GA as 2024-11-30 and needs no forced migration.
AI Search verbalizes images with the GenAI Prompt skill or embeds them with the Azure Vision or AML skill, and image descriptions in the Content Understanding skill need REST 2026-05-01-preview.
Azure Vision multimodal embeddings have 1,024 dimensions, images under 20 MB and 10 x 10 to 16,000 x 16,000 px, text of 1 to 70 words.
Cohere embed-v4.0 offers 256, 512, 1024 or 1536 (default) dimensions with 128k context; embed-v5.0-pro and -fast offer up to 2048 (default).
jina-embeddings-v4 has 3.8 billion parameters, single-vector and multi-vector output, and introduced Jina-VDR.
ColPali uses PaliGemma-3B with 1,024 patches projected to 128 dimensions and about 257.5 KB per page versus 8.6 KB for BGE-M3.
ColQwen2 caps patches at 768 and adds 5.3 nDCG@5 over ColPali.
The Content Safety image API accepts 4 MB, 50 x 50 to 7,200 x 7,200 px, and JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP, TIFF or WEBP.
The Content Safety image model returns severities 0, 2, 4 and 6, and the multimodal image-with-text model supports the full 0 to 7 scale.
Prompt Shields accepts prompts up to 10K characters and up to five documents totalling 10K characters, and detects user prompt attacks and document attacks.
Foundry guardrails moderate only the first 1,000 characters of text, and the Content Safety text API default maximum is 10K characters.
Azure Language native document PII redaction supports .txt, .pdf (including scanned PDFs) and .docx, and does not support digital images with embedded text.
Face identification and verification require registration, face detection does not, and Face recognition is prohibited for US police departments.
